title: Πρόβατον κειρόμενον
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 321. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Πρόβατον ἀφυῶς κειρόμενον πρὸς τὸν κείροντα ἔφη· « Εἰ μὲν ἔρια ζητεῖς, ἀνωτέρω τέμνε· εἰ δὲ κρεῶν ἐπιθυμεῖς, ἅπαξ με καταθύσας τοῦ κατὰ μικρὸν βασανίζειν ἀπάλλαξον. »
sentences.tr: Probaton aphyōs keiromenon pros ton keironta ephē· « Ei men eria zēteis, anōterō temne· ei de kreōn epithymeis, hapax me katathysas tou kata mikron basanizein apallaxon. »
sentences.l: A sheep being shorn unskilfully said to the one shearing it: « If you are seeking wool, cut higher up; but if you are longing for meat, having slaughtered me once for all, release me from the tormenting little by little. »
sentences.i: A sheep that was being clumsily shorn said to the shearer: « If it is wool you want, cut higher up; but if it is meat you are after, kill me once for all and be done with tormenting me by inches. »
sentences.n: εἰ μέν … εἰ δέ sets the two possible motives side by side, and the sheep offers a remedy for each. ἐπιθυμέω takes the genitive of what is desired (κρεῶν). τοῦ … βασανίζειν is an articular infinitive in the genitive after ἀπάλλαξον: verbs of releasing say what one is released from with the genitive. καταθύω is the word for slaughtering a victim, so the sheep offers itself as a sacrifice rather than endure the botched shearing.

sentences.t: Πρὸς τοὺς ἀφυῶς ταῖς τέχναις προσφερομένους ὁ λόγος ἁρμόδιός ἐστι.
sentences.tr: Pros tous aphyōs tais technais prospheromenous ho logos harmodios esti.
sentences.l: Against those who apply themselves to the crafts without aptitude the story is fitting.
sentences.i: The story fits those who take up a craft they have no aptitude for.
sentences.n: A closing formula of the same family as ὁ λόγος εὔκαιρος (fable 55) and ὁ λόγος ἁρμόζει (fables 62 and 108), here with the adjective ἁρμόδιος and the copula written out. προσφέρομαι in the middle takes the dative and means to bring oneself to a thing, to have dealings with it. ἀφυῶς repeats the first word said of the shearing: the moral is fastened to the story by that one adverb, 'without the natural gift for it'.
